findings.issue: The guide's opening sentence 'Where a step branches on plain values, the branch is a planner under # --- deciding a step on facts ---' and the section comment's 'So each place a step branches on plain values is a planner here' claim more than the code does. Branches on plain values still decided inline: advance's file-return arm `if stored_green(...) != _evio.STORED_HOLDS` (drive-phase.py:4301), `if tree: integrate_member(...)` (4385), kept_tree_stop / redo_patch at the top of advance, writer_wait/writer_settle, triage's review_due / filed-at-head / owed_tasks branches ahead of the advance point, drive_locked's `pending['decision'] == 'triage'` and `pending.get('task')` note_sessions branches, and sign-off. A reader told every plain-value branch is a planner would look for one that does not exist.
findings.resolution: Narrow both sentences to what is true, e.g. 'Four of the drive's branch points are planners under ...: advance's writer/scope/reviewer/gate/risk/close, the triage's advance and tail, drive_locked's stale and route, and close_task's findings/lock/route/commit/answer; the other branches (the file-return arm's stored-green check, integrate_member, kept_tree_stop, the triage's head and owed checks, sign-off) are still decided inline.' Apply the same narrowing to the comment at drive-phase.py:3910-3912.

intent.note: Task clause: 'Extract the decision seams S1-S4 in drive-phase.py into pure planners (_advance_plan, _triage_plan, _pending_turn, _close_plan) reading a facts dict; reads keep their order and their laziness'. The diff adds the four planners plus _fact/_at_point under '# --- deciding a step on facts ---' (drive-phase.py:3905-4199) and rewrites advance, close_task, triage and drive_locked to read facts and act on the arm. I compared every rewritten branch with HEAD (git show HEAD copy): writer (writer_holds read only when no executor return; after a filed writer return the point is asked again with holds False, then stale_brief, then the dispatched-executor mark, as HEAD), scope (scopeAccepted read only on a change), reviewer (mark read only when due and unfiled; session step; re-asked with stepped=True giving no-reviewer-return or, on a spent mark, the dispatch after the gate - `review_turn == 'dispatch'` is equivalent to HEAD's `due and reviewer is None` because HEAD returns no-reviewer-return whenever the mark survives the step), gate (stored_green read once, unconditionally, same predicate), risk (confirmed, then confirmed_in_advance, then standing_use only when not in advance - the journal-writing read stays behind the same conditions), close (signals/fix/plain, intent_basis strings byte-identical, gate_went_red only under fixes_only_lows), close_task (findings mark, lock_moved, writer_path_on and recorded_session lazy, own_commit only with no sha, review_items eager as before), triage (ctx.pop('advance') under the same condition, not-applied did-line appended before review_rounds is read, round-cap/triage sentences identical), drive_locked (keep/drop/usage-moved, note_sessions between the stale and route points as before, route order stop-other-task, advance-no-reason, advance, answer then onward, render, drive-task/drive-phase). The one reorder: verdict_moved is now read before state.pop('pending')/write_state; verdict_moved reads only the pending dict and ctx['basisNoted']/ctx['basisMoved'], and write_state writes only the state file while state.pop does not mutate the pending dict, so neither observes the other. Clause 'Add unit blocks up-block, ut-block, uq-block, uc-block ... one case per arm, both directions, literal expectations, no fixture repository': present in STAGES, every expectation is a written literal, every case pairs an arm with a one-fact-flipped twin, facts that must not be read are _never raisers; no repo is built. Clause 'PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md drive-phase section gains one paragraph naming the planners and why there is no single decide()': present at 4447, with the overclaim filed as finding 1. Clause 'The whole drive suite is green before and after': my one run of `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_drive_phase.py` exited 0, '1/1 files ok, 745 cases'. The executor's claim ('behaviour is unchanged'; reads listed as kept lazy; one reorder named) describes the diff in front of me.

intent.inheritedTestsBasis: tests.gate runs three single-suite commands: tests/test_drive_phase.py, tests/test__deps.py, tests/test__output_lints.py. I read the test_drive_phase.py end-to-end cases that reach the rewritten arms: hr1/hr2 (~6570, confirmed in advance vs. high-risk decision), sh1 in _standing_risk_cases (~6762, asserts risk.standing.used journal rows), the round-cap block (~6240-6295), the advance-needs-reason case (~4372), the usage-moved 'answers nothing' cases (~4364, ~4396) and the moved-basis case (~4086); each asserts the arm's output or its side effect, and none has a swallowing try, an empty filter or a does-not-raise shape that would survive the arm being deleted. test__deps.py and test__output_lints.py assert layer placement and house-style over the file, not drive behaviour; not read case by case.
